Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 77, verses 1–15:

This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 77, verses 25–28:

{25–28} That is: Did We not bestow favour upon you and grant you blessings by subjecting the earth to serve your interests, making it {a receptacle} for you: {for the living}, in their homes, {and for the dead}, in their graves? Then he mentioned the greatness of the sparks of the Fire, which indicates its immensity, its horror, and the ugliness of its appearance, saying: ﴿Indeed, it throws up sparks like the castle. This indicates that the Fire is dark in its flame, its embers, and its sparks, that it is black, repulsive in appearance, and intensely hot. This is a threat and warning to the deniers: even if they eat and drink in this world, enjoy its pleasures, and neglect acts of devotion, they are criminals who deserve what criminals deserve. Their pleasures will be cut off from them, and the consequences will remain upon them. Among their criminality is that when they are commanded to pray, which is the most noble of acts of worship, and it is said to them, ﴿Bow down,﴾ they refuse. What crime is greater than this? And what denial exceeds this? ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾ Among the woe upon them is that the doors of success are closed to them and they are deprived of every good. When they deny this Qur'an, which is the highest level of truthfulness and certainty in absolute terms, ﴿then in what statement after it will they believe?﴾ Will it be in falsehood, which is as its name indicates, and on which no doubt stands, let alone evidence? Or in the words of a polytheist, a great liar, a fabricator, a manifest deceiver? After the clear light there is nothing but the darkest darknesses, and after the truth upon which clear proofs and decisive demonstrations stand, there is nothing but blatant fabrication and manifest lying, which befits none but those who resemble it. So woe to them, how blind they are! Alas for them, how lost and wretched they are! We ask Allah for pardon and well-being; He is Generous and Bountiful.
